question.text: A <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>0</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>4</mn><mo> </mo><mi>kg</mi></math> mass takes <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>8</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi></math> to reach ground when dropped from a certain height <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>P</mi></math> above surface of earth. The loss of potential energy in the last second of fall is ______ <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">J</mi></math>. [Take <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>g</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>10</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup></math>]

solution.text:
Displacement in nth second is given by Sn=u+a22n-1

Here, displacement is 8th second is

S8=0+12×10×(2×8-1)

⇒S8=75 m

Loss of potential energy is 

ΔU=mgS8=0.4×10×75

⇒ΔU=300 J.
